review:
Game is transitioning to F2P and the devs are giving full refunds!

As a consumer that is amazing!

But I feel I've got my money's worth from the game so I will not be refunding.

Mad respect to the dev!
By far the only devs i've seen that gives a refund for abandoned games. All other devs and publishers should learn the lesson. For that alone, I give it a thumbs up.

There is a lot of potential here, but the advertised solo play doesn't work as a viable gameplay option. AI teammates and controls (changing angles/giving orders/managing multiple floors) do not enable solid campaign play, and the PVE skimrish option doesn't implement AI companions at all. There is a lot that is really brilliant here, but if you are interested in single player it just isn't ready technically or in terms of content.

[h1]TL;DR:

This game is abandonware, the devs released their last update and it almost feels like a scam, save your money, this game is not at all worth it, even on sale![/h1]

[hr][/hr]

[b][i]I absolutely loved this game, especially the multiplayer aspect, I spent just over 60 hours playing mainly the multiplayer (because the ai in singleplayer was total garbage) alone or with friends and enjoyed pretty much every second of it. But unfortunately from the development team's behaviour surrounding updates and adding in the modding tool I knew something was amiss and so did a lot of other people, the game soon became almost entirely abandoned by the playerbase and it was a rarity to see other players online.

As of writing, I just woke up on the morning of August 12th in Australia, not long after the devs released their final update (in their own words) on the 11th I'm assuming US time. They say they're happy with the state the game is in, but I don't think that's true and I know the community doesn't feel that is true as recent reviews are "Very Negative" and overall reviews are "Mostly Positive", down from being "Overwhelmingly Positive". For whatever reason it seems the devs never had the drive to support this game right from the start and from now on it is abandonware.

I believed with all my heart that this game could become very popular and was something special. It was for a time, but unfortunately that short period is over and I cannot recommend anyone buy this game, it's almost at the point where I'd call it a scam. I doubt the AI has changed, so even as a singleplayer title it is not worth $28.95 AUD.[/i]

Giving full refunds for a game goes F2P is something you never hear about in this day and age.

For those who have issues with the refunds, the refund process guide they posted in their announcements should help with the refunding

For what its worth the devs stuck by their word and even plowed through to get the refunds for players despite the refund problems, so for that, I give them a thumbs up.

It's like someone took XCOM 2012, Doorkickers, Insurgency, Rainbow Six, SWAT 4 and some random twin stick shooter and put them all into a blender.

Sadly seems like it's not gonna get updated any more. Unlike some people, I'm not gonna flip this review to negative because it's not like the game isn't fun...
But yeah keep in mind that what you see here is all you get.

I wish Steam allowed a "Meh" button when asking if I'd recommend this game. It seems more like a "proof of concept" than a game, even if it feels finished and polished.

On the good side you have: 
[list]
[*]A great gameplay (better than any other isometrical tactical shooter that I know of. If you do know of something better, or on par, please comment below, since I'll be interested in playing).
[*]Beautiful, detailed assets.
[*]A great variety of weapons, equipment, and skins, all of them freely available as you level up.
[*]Every weapong feels unique. There are some that excel over the rest (for example, the AS-VAL), but you can play mostly with any weapon you like, and be efficient.
[*]A nice-ish balance, even on PvP.
[*]A great, albeit short, single player/4 Players coop campaign.
[*]Almost no bugs (I really can't remember a single one, though I'm sure there has to be some).
[*]Modding tools.
[/list]
On the bad side:
[list]
[*]The devs said that the game is finished, so they won't be adding new content or fixing issues. Basically, we are on our own.
[*]Allied AI would greatly benefit if you could give them complex orders (SWAT style).
[*]The lack of content is appalling.
[*]Since the devs have abandoned their game, the community seems to have abandoned it also, so expect no new modded content, and almost empty MP/COOP lobbies.
[*][strike]Using ANY kind of modded content prevents you from gaining XP, so you have to choose between using that nice Desert Eagle mod (which is pretty well balanced, on my opinion) or keep unlocking native assets, including guns.[/strike]As pointed out by a dev, this is no longer the case and mods can be used freely.
[*]AI, specially allied AI, can be extremely frustrating.
[/list]

As it is, I can only recommend the game if you have a group of friends to play the coop campaign, or play some MP matches amongst yourselves. Also, if you find it on sale, you can give it a try. But, see right there near my name, that I have 25 hours? That's the game's life expectancy. Bear that in mind. Then again, there is nothing even remotely comparable to this in terms of gameplay, so I'd recommend based solely on that fact.

What happened to this game? I'll explain it from my pov. The game at launch was awesome, it was really fun. To me it kinda felt like it had potential to be a top down "tarkov" game and I loved it. It still is fun to some extent now tbh. Fun PvE and fun PvP, BUT... everything was too short at launch. Short campaign (8 missions or so that were like 20 mins each without any replayability), few maps, few rewards, gun balance issues on PvP and no modding tools at launch because they were delayed (which they said would be released at launch)....

The game quickly ran out of content at launch and people were asking the devs what they were planning with the game and they were never really willing to share any informations or any kind of "roadmaps" with the community. They kept relatively quiet on this front other than saying they were working on modding tools (which took a few months to actually release after the launch) and people got upset with them for not sharing anything else. As if they had no plans at all.

It quickly soured the community because most players started thinking that all they wanted was for modders to take over and make content for the game instead of them actually doing content once the modding tools would be released and that they'd abandon the game after. By the time they had released the modding tools, most of the community that played the game had moved on to other games. It took them too long to release the tools.

After that people kept asking whats the futur of the game and even with the playerbase dwindling very quickly, the devs kept absolutely quiet on their plans. As if it was a state secret or whatever. For the remaining few people that played the game at that point, when they saw there was nothing to look for, they also started to leave the game.

There was essentially no one playing the game anymore after a few months. It was eventually announced that the devs would stop developping/working on the game. Officially leaving it as is (AKA abandoning it) and making it "dead game". 

Theres no updates anymore, barely anyone plays this anymore and its a very short game. I believe if I remember right, you can beat the game within 3 hours if you're quick enough. I also believe the devs are still hanging around.

Now, they have decided to make the game F2P for everyone and to their credit, they are offering refunds to everyone who purchased the game, which is awesome. Atleast we can get our money back. Considering it is F2P now, id say you can play the short campaign, have a good time and then move on to other things too. It's not a bad game, it's fun. It's just abandoned and dead. And when I say "abandoned", I dont mean its not finished. The game is fully playable. I just mean theres no more updates, DLC or planned content from the devs.

With the game being F2P in mind now, even though the game has a poor history, I can "somewhat" recommend it. If the game still had a pricetag though, I would absolutely not recommend it. But now that its F2P, I can recommend it. Its fun, it works and I guess you can mod it if you want. Just know that theres no official support from the devs anymore. So you get what you see.

So the developers just released their last patch for the game. A lot of people in the official discord and steam reviews are calling this game a scam and abandon-ware. As somebody who has owned this game since the first week of launch and have rode with it for most of it's lifetime I disagree with these statements. For 20 dollars this game is actually pretty good, I enjoy what they were trying to do here with it being a top down tactical shooter. Yes, one of the biggest selling points was mod support and they delayed it a bunch of times and we finally got it when it was basically too little too late. I get the frustration and I agree that the devs scuffed the post-launch phase of this game hardcore. However with that in mind when I went into buying this game I considered what was already present in TTO rather what was coming in the future. For 20 dollars this game is easily worth it.

This game launched with an excellent core. The big selling point was mod support and how you could easily build nearly anything in this game. The community was excited, the basics were there and while there wasn't a ton of content it was easy to see how user generated content would make this a sleeper.

Except a couple weeks before release mod tools were delayed, okay. The message was they had to do a little more work. That was in November. It's February 9th. There's still no mod tools, and it's increasingly apparent from the company's comments on reddit and hypothesis of users that they are in a legal quagmire and knew they couldn't release them in the first place. 

Rather than being transparent that this wasn't a technical delay, they made it sound like these tools were around the corner and sold a bunch of copies in December.

Really, really shameful business practice. So much potential here and flushed down the toilet by a lack of integrity.

As is, if you were hoping for a tactical single player experience I would not recommend this.

The control you have over your squad mates in not precise enough to do even basic things like breach a room at the same time, or move in after a flash bang goes off. Squad mates will also not listen to orders to stay in cover, sometimes just wandering off to do their own thing once the shooting starts. They will even try to find cover on the other side of an enemy position, breaking stealth and or even failing the mission.

Was hoping for something close to a top-down SOCOM-like experience, but this unfortunately isn't it. There are so many cool features here and it's so close to being fantastic. Maybe the co-op is a different story.

Try this if you're having difficulty adjusting to the camera angle

Settings --> controls
"Top Deadzone: 15
Bottom Deadzone: 20 
Change camera view with caps"
                        -KodeMan 2021

This will make the games camera angle lean more towards whats in The Division, but camera angle seems to be more on personal preferences.
Apart from adjusting the camera angle this game is really solid and I had a lot of fun pushing objectives with a random squad I met in a quick join lobby. The arcade mode is more run and gun fun, while the realism mode forces you to stick together, cover angles and play slower (in PvE). The two separate difficulties help choose what type of game play you're looking for. 
Overall 8/10: great game, many small interesting tactical features. Still a new game, more content and balancing will come in time

First thoughts after just about 1:30h

Secondly, your a.i. teammates are... well...let's say they serve as a meat shield at any rate > they desperately need finer/better controls - if you expect Door Kickers levels of control, you'll find this pretty basic when it comes to coordination. 
I do understand that the a.i. supposedly "acts natural" when left alone, BUT your mates often times just stand around idly in the open field if not ordered around or they will swoop in right in front of your muzzle at the most unfortunate times. 

Graphics are nice, sound seems pretty decent too, so far. 
General controls are fine (except camera, in my opinion).
Mission design is quite nice, too. There's a lot more option than the ones you see at first glance which gives each Op a good replay value.
Realism Mode is a no brainer - don't even bother with Arcade if you've played Door Kickers 1 and/or 2 before. 
With Realism Mode turned on, the game is very tough and quite punishing - consider me satisfied.
Very happy with the purchase thus far, since my only real gripes are with camera control and occasionally dumb a.i.

Will test online co-op soon - for now I'd love the option for Lone Wolf mode in the campaign (maybe I missed this?)

I’ve only ever played the singleplayer so that is what this review will be center around. The “AI” ruins this game plain and simple. The bad AI kills any and almost all enjoyment that you can get from this game. First the friendly AI will actively not follow orders, I can stop right there. How be you execute any sort of plan or tactic if simple orders will not be followed? Your squadmates will do any and everything save what you’ve asked. They will run in front of your barrel. They will turn their back to the enemy while being actively engaged. You cannot issue ROE to fire at will, AI will only return fire. They do not know how to clear a room. One person will breach a room and just stand in the middle of the room. They do provide any type of assistance to each other unless one of them is downed. I could go on and on but you get the idea, friendly AI bad.

The enemy AI is just as bad. They never operate as a unit but a group of individuals. Using numbers to overwhelm you which will lead you to use cheesy tactics like funneling and kiting.

Long story short is that this is not a good game. I could talk about the gameplay and story but fixing those things and not dealing with the AI would not change much.

The game is really fun. It has been said that it combines some of the best elements of Escape from Tarkov, Arma, and Doorkickers. I agree with this viewpoint. If this is something which appeals to you, I suggest that you buy the game.

The campaign is good and steadily ramps up in difficulty. Upon a certain point however, your AI squadmates become more of liability to your progress as their threat response AI shows its limitation. 

For example, they will hunker next to a boulder on a particular angle, will receive fire from an enfilade position, and not respond to the fire. Or they will take fire from targets that appear in and out of vision (stealth), neither probing the attacker or returning fire in the target's direction.

The weapons are fun and reasonably varied. My only criticisms are that they all sound like they are being fired with a silencer, and that the marksmen rifles feel like poor choices. This could be an impression developed from my playstyle, however I feel their body shots don't deal enough damage and the way the recoil affects the accuracy via the swirly reticle mechanic means you forfeit too much time to lay the next shot.

What I'd like to see from the game is a mix of quality life features and new content. The ability to remove camo from apparel would be appreciated, especially for a particular set of Russian clothes. As nice as the surprise of new unlocks is, it'd also be useful to know what you unlock at each profile level rather than scrolling through all options. Information about whether accessories have an in-game effect would be appreciated, e.g. NVG - they actually work. Does it confer an advantage, even in caves with all the lights disabled? From what I've observed no, it's purely a visual effect. Do the headsets confer a benefit in game other than looking cool? Can't say.

New guns and new missions are the content I desire. I'd happily pay for DLC at this point. The ability to invite players to join in your campaign missions would be a great nice-to-have as well, however I'd prize further content above this.

So, let me start it with this might be the best game to not be given much of a chance. Thunder Tier One is an isometric shooter with an emphasis on tactics. In short, it's basically what you get if you take something like Grim Dawn, set it in the Cold War/modern day, and made it more tactical than Rainbow Six: Siege and Ghost Recon Breakpoint combined. This is a game I've always wanted to have but it fell short on what I'd like to see, but more on that later.

From the start, the game is isometric and this could present the worst aspect of the game in terms of attracting an audience. This, however, is a bit sad as the game, as I already stated, manages to be far more tactical and in depth than various mainstream "tactical" games. I was actually blown away by how well this game managed that. I can't really give this game ANY criticism in those regards, and the camera angle doesn't detract from this at all. In fact the game did a great job in making it an important aspect of the game. You can pan around to a degree but unless you have line of sight with an enemy, they won't show up. This is great. You can actually sneak around and enemies can sneak up on you. I love it!

Again, the tactics aspect of the game is great too. I've no complaints that come to mind, outside of maybe that it'd be nice if camouflage actually worked towards making enemies have a harder time spotting/detecting you. However, that might be something that can be fixed, more on that later.

Levels... some players have added more, and with that I'm going to touch on what I said above. ANYTHING this game thus far lacks can be added with mods, to which there are... some. New maps, gear, cosmetics, missions, etc. The problem is once the mod tool dropped, the Workshop didn't get a whole tidal wave of content like I was hoping for. Sure, what's currently available IS very good, but it's still underwhelming overall. This leads into the reason, and the main problem with the game right now.

The population is beyond dwindling. The game averages 15 players a month. It started strong but I think the length of time it took to get the mod tool out was too long and by the time it dropped enthusiasm and interest in the game had already gone cold. Which is sad, the game is VERY unique and has MASSIVE potential, especially as the mod tool allows you to do so much. (In theory)

I recommend this game, but know that sadly there's not much of a population for it anymore. Playing it with friends could be GREAT fun, and if you can use the mod tool to add awesome things, do it. I wish this game would get a revival, it's very underrated. In fact, while typing this, I won't lie in saying I played it again, checked the population, and uninstalled it only to type this while feeling a bit depressed over how abandoned this game is by the players. It's been a few months since the last dev notes, but in all honesty I can't blame them with how low player numbers are, and with how players can add content if they want more. If I knew how, I'd do it myself.

It's an easy recommend for free, but even when it was $20 US I considered it worth it. There's zero online population, though, so you'll have to bring your own friends. One or two will get you through most of the game, but if you want to survive the last few levels you'll need at least three.
